\section{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- General}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.General
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- General: Introduction}
Coordinate hypercontractivity tensorizes on heterogeneous finite probability products. Both conjugate hypercontractive estimates are obtained at the sharp discrete radius and at the minimum-atom radius.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- General: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Tensorization above the first moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction_gt_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteTensorization.norm_tensorization}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, and let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$1\le p$, $1<q$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and every
real-valued function $g$ on that coordinate, the function $x\mapsto \rho
g(x)+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_i g$ has $q$-moment norm at most the $p$-moment norm of $g$, with
respect to the coordinate weights of $P$. Then every real-valued function $f$ on the
product outcome space satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le \|f\|_{p,P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product hypercontractivity by tensorization]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_norm_one_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction_gt_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, and let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$1\le p\le q$ and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and every
real-valued function $g$ on that coordinate, the function $x\mapsto \rho
g(x)+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_i g$ has $q$-moment norm at most the $p$-moment norm of $g$,
where expectation and norms use the coordinate weights of $P$. Then for every
real-valued function $f$ on the product outcome space, $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le
\|f\|_{p,P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Taking square roots of moment bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_norm_le_of_sq_moments}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $A,B,p,q\in\mathbb R$ with $A,B\ge0$. If $A^{2/q}\le B^{2/p}$, then $A^{1/q}\le
B^{1/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of quadratic noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_noise_quadratic_mono}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i\in\bbr$ satisfying $w_i\ge0$ for every $i$ and
$\sum_{i\in I}w_i=1$. For $\rho,\sigma\in\bbr$ with $0\le\rho\le\sigma$ and any
$g:I\to\bbr$, one has $\rho^2\sum_{i\in I}w_i g_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_{i\in I}w_i
g_i)^2\le\sigma^2\sum_{i\in I}w_i g_i^2+(1-\sigma^2)(\sum_{i\in I}w_i g_i)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp finite-coordinate hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_coordinate_hypercontractivity_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_duality, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_identities, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_sharp_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_noise_quadratic_mono, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_norm_le_of_sq_moments, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i\in\bbr$ satisfying $\sum_{i\in I}w_i=1$. Let
$\lambda,q,\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $0<\lambda<1/2$, $w_i\ge\lambda$ for every $i\in I$,
$q>2$, $0\le\rho$, and $\rho\le\rho_*(q,\lambda)$, where
$\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$ and
$u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. For every $g:I\to\bbr$, both weighted norm inequalities
hold: $\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}w_i|\rho g_i+(1-\rho)\sum_{j\in
I}w_jg_j|^q\bigr)^{1/q}\le\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}w_i|g_i|^2\bigr)^{1/2}$ and
$\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}w_i|\rho g_i+(1-\rho)\sum_{j\in
I}w_jg_j|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}w_i|g_i|^{q/(q-1)}\bigr)^{(q-1)/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp hypercontractivity for product spaces]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_coordinate_hypercontractivity_sharp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction_gt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$
satisfy $0<\lambda<1/2$ and $q>2$. Suppose every coordinate atom has weight at least
$\lambda$. Define $u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$ and
$r=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$. If $0\le\rho\le r$, then every real-valued
function $f$ on the product outcome space satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$
and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for a hyperbolic sine ratio]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sinh_ratio_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<a\le b$. Then $\frac{a}{b}e^{a-b}\le\frac{\sinh
a}{\sinh b}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse radius bounded by the sharp radius]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coarse_radius_le_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sinh_ratio_lower_bound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $q,\lambda\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1$, and set
$u=\log\bigl((1-t)/t\bigr)$ when defining $r(q,t)=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$.
Then $\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}\le r\bigl(q,\lambda/(1+\lambda)\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hypercontractive bounds for unit atoms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_atom_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with coordinate atom weights at least $1$,
and let $q>2$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f$ be a real-valued function on its product
outcome space. Then the product noise operator satisfies both $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le
\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le \|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hypercontractivity on Finite Product Spaces]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coarse_radius_le_sharp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_atom_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_sharp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights,
and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$. Assume $0<\lambda\le1$, every coordinate atom has
weight at least $\lambda$, $q>2$, and $\rho\ge0$ with $\rho\le
\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$. Then every real-valued function $f$ on the product space
satisfies both $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho
f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-coordinate hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_coordinate_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of one finite probability space with strictly positive atom weights
summing to one, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\lambda\le1$, $q>2$, and
$0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$. Assume every atom of $P$ has weight at least
$\lambda$. For every real-valued function $f$ on the outcome space, both $\|T_\rho
f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ hold, where
$T_\rho$ is the product spectral noise operator and the norms are the corresponding

\end{theorem}
